label: sec:theory
title: The Theory of Parametric Bit-vectors
html: The theory of parametric bit-vectors TPBV​=(ΣPBV​,IPBV​) was introduced in [7] as a formalization of the parametric bit-vectors of [28] in which bit-widths are first-class integer terms. Its signature ΣPBV​ (Table 1) extends ΣIA​ with a single new sort PBV, whose domain is the set of all bit-vectors of all positive widths, with parametric variants of the SMT-LIB 2 bit-vector operators (arithmetic, bitwise, shift, comparison, concatenation, extraction and extension), and with two new symbols: ∣␣∣, which maps a bit-vector to its width, and to-pbv, which maps integers n>0 and m to the bit-vector of width n representing mmod2n and thereby models parametric constants (e.g., to-pbv(k,0) is the bit-vector of k zeros). Width-changing operators take their width arguments as integer terms, e.g., x[i:j] and extz​(n,x), and are interpreted arbitrarily outside their intended domain. Since PBV is a single sort, ΣPBV​ admits terms such as x∘x+Bx that are ill-sorted for every choice of widths. Such spurious interpretations are excluded by the notion of admissible satisfiability: a function Adm collects, while traversing a formula φ, the constraints that every operator imposes on the (symbolic) widths of its arguments, expressed via a function Bw that computes an integer term for the width of a term (e.g., BW(x∘y)=∣x∣+∣y∣), and φ is admissibly TPBV​-satisfiable if it is satisfied by a TPBV​-interpretation that also satisfies ADM(φ). This is the notion of satisfiability that the solver decides. For formal definitions and examples, we refer to [7, Sect. 3]. We call the integer constraints on the widths of a formula, i.e., its integer literals over widths together with ADM(φ), its width constraints, and say that a condition is entailed if it follows from them. A formula is single-width if all of its bit-vector terms have the same symbolic width, and multi-width if it involves several width parameters, which are combined by extraction, extension and concatenation.
